title: Milky Way Dynamics Favor Dark Matter over Modified Gravity Models (Wang et al.)
efc_relevance: Joint reconstruction of the Milky Way radial rotation curve, Gaia vertical phase-space spirals, and a broken-exponential stellar disk shows that no modified-gravity model can simultaneously reproduce radial and vertical fields — MOND is disfavoured at >13σ and STVG at >4σ, while a standard DM halo fits all three observables. Tightens the discriminator band for any framework that aspires to reproduce galactic dynamics without a particle-DM halo (framework:MOND-Milgrom1983, framework:TeVeS-Bekenstein2004, framework:RMOND-Skordis2021, framework:MassToHorizon-2025, framework:VerlindeEmergent-2016). EFC's S(r,t) source-term must reproduce both radial RC and vertical phase-space spirals jointly; this paper sets the empirical bar.
ledger_action: Add to External Research Ledger under cluster modified-gravity-vs-dm; update framework rows MOND-Milgrom1983 (>13σ MW tension), TeVeS-Bekenstein2004, RMOND-Skordis2021, MassToHorizon-2025, and VerlindeEmergent-2016 with the joint radial+vertical-field discriminator note; new gap row (gap predictions-mw-vertical-spirals-efc) — EFC currently has no published prediction for the Gaia vertical-spiral amplitude at the Solar neighbourhood; required follow-up: compute EFC S(r,t) contribution to the disk gravitational field K_z(z) and overlay on the Wang et al. constraint band.
